'''Claude André Pruneau''' (born November 9, 1960) is a Canadian-American experimental high-energy nuclear physicist. He is a professor of physics at [[Wayne State University]] and the author of several books. He is best known for his work on particle correlation measurements in [[heavy-ion collision]]s at the [[Relativistic Heavy Ion Collider]] (RHIC) and the [[Large Hadron Collider]] (LHC).

== Early life and education ==
Pruneau is a French-Canadian native born in [[Quebec City]]. He attended Collège des Jésuites and Cégep de Sainte-Foy before studying at [[Université Laval]], where he earned a B.Sc. in 1982, an M.Sc. in 1983, and a Ph.D. in physics in 1987.<ref name="WSUprofile">{{cite web |title=Claude Pruneau |url=https://clasprofiles.wayne.edu/profile/aa7526 |publisher=Wayne State University, College of Liberal Arts and Sciences |access-date=September 7, 2026}}</ref><ref name="ORCID">{{cite web |title=Claude Pruneau |url=https://orcid.org/0000-0002-0458-538X |website=ORCID |access-date=September 7, 2026}}</ref> His doctoral advisor was Claude St-Pierre.<ref name="INSPIRE">{{cite web |title=Claude A. Pruneau |url=https://inspirehep.net/authors/992685 |website=INSPIRE-HEP |access-date=September 7, 2026}}</ref>

== Career ==
After his Ph.D., Pruneau was a research associate at the Chalk River Nuclear Laboratories of [[Atomic Energy of Canada Limited]] from 1987 to 1989 and then at [[McGill University]] from 1989 to 1991.<ref name="WSUprofile" /> He joined the Wayne State University faculty in 1992 as an assistant professor (research), became assistant professor in 1993, associate professor in 1998, and professor in 2004.<ref name="WSUprofile" /><ref name="ORCID" />

He conducts research on the search for and study of the [[quark–gluon plasma]] (QGP) at [[Brookhaven National Laboratory]] and [[CERN]]. He has been a visiting professor at the [[Indian Institute of Technology Bombay]].<ref name="WSUprofile" />

== Research ==
Pruneau's research focuses on the experimental study of the quark–gluon plasma, a [[state of matter]] believed to have existed microseconds after the [[Big Bang]]. His work has been carried out in large international collaborations, including early experiments at the Brookhaven [[Alternating Gradient Synchrotron]] (E814, E877, and E864), the [[STAR experiment]] at RHIC, and the [[ALICE experiment]] at the LHC.<ref name="INSPIRE" /><ref name="WSUprofile" />

=== Shear viscosity of the quark–gluon plasma ===
One of his contributions is the extraction of the specific [[shear viscosity]] ({{math|''η''/''s''}}) of the QGP. In a 2021 paper in ''[[The European Physical Journal C]]'', Pruneau and collaborators used the progressive longitudinal broadening of transverse-momentum two-particle correlations measured by STAR and ALICE to estimate this transport coefficient.<ref name="eta2021">{{cite journal |last1=Gonzalez |first1=V. |last2=Basu |first2=S. |last3=Marin |first3=A. |last4=Pan |first4=J. |last5=Ladron de Guevara |first5=P. |last6=Pruneau |first6=C. A. |title=Extraction of the specific shear viscosity of quark-gluon plasma from two-particle transverse momentum correlations |journal=The European Physical Journal C |volume=81 |issue=5 |article-number=465 |year=2021 |doi=10.1140/epjc/s10052-021-09260-z |arxiv=2012.10542 |doi-access=free}}</ref> The analysis indicated that the QGP behaves as a nearly "perfect liquid", with {{math|''η''/''s''}} approaching the theoretical Kovtun–Son–Starinets bound. Estimates based on ALICE data showed little centrality dependence at LHC energy, while STAR data at top RHIC energy suggested a possible centrality dependence.<ref name="eta2021" />

=== Balance functions ===
In 2023 he and collaborators introduced a unified formulation of general balance functions that can accommodate electric charge as well as strange, baryon, charm, and bottom quantum numbers, and that distinguishes acceptance-independent definitions from experimentally bound measurements.<ref name="UBF2023">{{cite journal |last1=Pruneau |first1=Claude |last2=Gonzalez |first2=Victor |last3=Hanley |first3=Brian |last4=Marin |first4=Ana |last5=Basu |first5=Sumit |title=Accounting for nonvanishing net-charge with unified balance functions |journal=Physical Review C |volume=107 |issue=1 |article-number=014902 |year=2023 |doi=10.1103/PhysRevC.107.014902 |arxiv=2209.10420}}</ref> Subsequent work formalized multiparticle integral and differential correlation functions and multiparticle balance functions,<ref name="Multi2024">{{cite journal |last1=Pruneau |first1=Claude |last2=Gonzalez |first2=Victor |last3=Marin |first3=Ana |last4=Basu |first4=Sumit |title=Multiparticle integral and differential correlation functions |journal=Physical Review C |volume=109 |issue=4 |article-number=044904 |year=2024 |doi=10.1103/PhysRevC.109.044904|doi-access=free }}</ref> and applied mixed-species charge and baryon balance functions in PYTHIA studies of proton–proton collisions.<ref name="Mixed2024">{{cite journal |last1=Pruneau |first1=Claude |last2=Basu |first2=Sumit |last3=Gonzalez |first3=Victor |last4=Hanley |first4=Brian |last5=Marin |first5=Ana |last6=Dobrin |first6=Alexandru F. |last7=Manea |first7=Alexandru |title=Mixed-species charge and baryon balance functions studies with PYTHIA |journal=Physical Review C |volume=109 |issue=6 |article-number=064913 |year=2024 |doi=10.1103/PhysRevC.109.064913 |arxiv=2403.13007}}</ref> A 2025 paper in ''The European Physical Journal C'' used balance functions in PYTHIA 8 and EPOS4 simulations to constrain late-stage particle-production mechanisms in proton–proton collisions.<ref name="Manea2025">{{cite journal |last1=Manea |first1=Alexandru |last2=Pruneau |first2=Claude |last3=Brandibur |first3=Diana Catalina |last4=Danu |first4=Andrea |last5=Dobrin |first5=Alexandru F. |last6=Gonzalez |first6=Victor |last7=Basu |first7=Sumit |title=Investigating late-stage particle production in pp collisions with balance functions |journal=The European Physical Journal C |volume=85 |article-number=323 |year=2025 |doi=10.1140/epjc/s10052-025-14049-5 |arxiv=2411.11207 |doi-access=free}}</ref>

=== Analysis methods and software ===
Pruneau developed an identity method for measurements of multiplicity moments and fluctuation observables when particle identification is incomplete.<ref name="Identity2017">{{cite journal |last=Pruneau |first=Claude A. |title=Identity method reexamined |journal=Physical Review C |volume=96 |issue=5 |article-number=054902 |date=November 3, 2017 |doi=10.1103/PhysRevC.96.054902 |arxiv=1706.01333}}</ref> Within the STAR collaboration he was part of a team that created the track-reconstruction software used to convert raw detector data into kinematic quantities for physics analysis.<ref name="WSUprofile" />

== Books ==
Pruneau is the author of the graduate textbook ''Data Analysis Techniques for Physical Scientists'' (Cambridge University Press, 2017), a treatment of probability, statistics, correlation measurements, unfolding, and Monte Carlo methods aimed at experimental physical scientists.<ref name="DATPS">{{cite book |last=Pruneau |first=Claude A. |title=Data Analysis Techniques for Physical Scientists |publisher=Cambridge University Press |year=2017 |isbn=978-1-108-41678-8 |doi=10.1017/9781108241922}}</ref> The book received reviews in ''[[Contemporary Physics]]'', ''[[Physics Today]]'', and ''Computing Reviews''.<ref>{{cite journal |last=Harker |first=A. H. |title=Review of Data Analysis Techniques for Physical Scientists |journal=Contemporary Physics |volume=59 |issue=2 |pages=218 |year=2018 |doi=10.1080/00107514.2018.1448452}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |last=Martin-Hein |first=Emilie |title=Mathematical tools to tame big data |journal=Physics Today |volume=71 |issue=8 |pages=54–55 |year=2018 |doi=10.1063/PT.3.4000}}</ref>

He also co-authored Wayne State special editions of the introductory textbook ''Foundations of Astronomy'' (Cengage), with Michael A. Seeds and Dana Backman. The custom editions, used in Wayne State's AST 2010 course, appeared in 2013, 2014, and 2016 and incorporated additional chapters prepared for a planned companion text, ''Exploring Astronomy''.<ref name="WSUprofile" />
